title: Timelines, Sentences, Threads, Energy, Specs
description: Five interfaces whose behaviour lives in something readable: a timeline, a layout as sentences, a scan, an energy field, a spec.

drops.title: The Launch Screen Is a Timeline
drops.description: Three app welcome sequences torn down to their tracks — a mask reveal, staggered springs, and a splash that holds then cuts hard.
drops.concept: The original is a teardown of how top apps say hello, rebuilding each launch sequence as an authored timeline on a fixed reference canvas, with a replay key and a reduced-motion path that jumps to the final state. This version re-authors three of those patterns as plain track lists over DOM layers: a blink into an expanding circular mask, a crossfade followed by per-asset staggered springs, and a splash that holds on a pulsing dot before a hard cut. A ruler under each phone shows every track as a bar with a live playhead.

interaction.mouse: Scrub the playhead to move all three sequences together, or change the playback speed.
interaction.click: Click any phone — or the replay button — to restart the sequences from zero.
interaction.touch: Tap a phone to replay; the three screens stack on narrow viewports.

drops.title: The Layout Is Written Down
drops.description: A diagram language where each statement says where its box goes — and the renderer draws exactly that, warnings and all.
drops.concept: No auto-layout, no force simulation. Boxes are placed by relations written in the file — right of, below, even with, with an explicit gap — and the engine never moves a box to make room or routes a line around one. When the result may not read as intended it still draws it and prints a one-line warning with the location and size of the problem, which the third preset demonstrates on purpose. The pipeline is the original's three stages: a parser, a placement pass and an SVG renderer.

interaction.mouse: Edit the source on the left and the diagram re-renders as you type; the gap slider changes every unqualified gap.
interaction.click: Load any of the three example files, including one written to overlap.
interaction.touch: The editor and diagram stack vertically; the diagram pane scrolls if the drawing is wider than the screen.

drops.title: Letters Woven From Threads
drops.description: Each pixel column of a word becomes a filament that runs straight through the letter and bends flat at both ends.
drops.concept: The original builds its alphabet from sheets of parallel threads that bend at each end, solved per pixel in a WebGL 2 fragment shader. This version scans a rendered word column by column, turns each column into a thread with its own hash-driven brightness, and draws the bends as quadratic curves splaying away above and below. A travelling swell lights the weave; the paths are batched into twelve brightness buckets so the whole thing is a handful of strokes per frame.

interaction.mouse: Type any word to reweave all three materials; sliders change density, speed, light reach and splay.
interaction.click: Click into the field and type — the weave rebuilds on every keystroke.
interaction.touch: The on-screen keyboard works the same way; three material rows stack on narrow screens.

drops.title: The Edge of the Window Answers
drops.description: A neon ring hugs the viewport and carries state in its own light — taps, keystrokes and saves all land somewhere on it.
drops.concept: Rather than a toast or a spinner, feedback is pushed into the edge of the window itself. Energy is added at a point, projected to the nearest edge, where it forms a Gaussian hotspot that decays; keystrokes land on a column of the bottom edge with a faster decay, and a save sends an ambient pulse all the way round. Colour comes from a 256-entry lookup table cycling around the ring, and typing shortens its rotation from eight seconds to three.
tech: Sampled rounded-rect ring with inward normals
Gaussian energy hotspots with exponential decay

interaction.mouse: Tap anywhere and the energy appears on the nearest edge; sliders change inset, band depth, core width and decay.
interaction.click: Save sends a pulse around the whole ring; Kindle spreads a wavefront out from the button in both directions.
interaction.touch: Tapping works the same; typing in the note lights a column on the bottom edge and speeds the palette up.

drops.title: Charts Are a Spec, Not a Drawing
drops.description: Three charts built from small JSON specs in plain SVG: they draw in, tween from where they already are, and answer the keyboard.
drops.concept: Every mark is an SVG element placed from a spec of type, data, encoding and options — no chart library and no canvas. The charts draw in when they scroll into view with a per-mark stagger, and when the data changes they tween from their current positions rather than restarting, which the New data button shows. Each one supports arrow-key navigation, a live readout, a drag-over-a-range summary on the trend chart, and a hidden data table for screen readers.
tech: Keyboard navigation and SR data table

interaction.mouse: Hover a bar or a wedge for a readout; drag across the trend line to get the change, high and low for that range.
interaction.click: New data retargets every chart mid-flight; Replay resets the marks and plays the staggered draw-in again.
interaction.touch: Touch and drag works on all three; the keyboard path is available once a chart is focused.
